senses.sense_definition: Difficult to understand or grasp; abstruse and profound.

examples.text: The professor wrote a <w>recondite</w> paper on ancient mathematical theories that few students could follow.
He spent his entire career studying <w>recondite</w> subjects that held little interest for the general public.

senses.sense_definition: Little known or understood by most people; esoteric or secret.

examples.text: The author filled his novel with <w>recondite</w> references that only a dedicated scholar would recognize.
She possessed a vast collection of <w>recondite</w> knowledge about forgotten historical events.

senses.sense_definition: Hidden or removed from view; deep-seated or concealed.

examples.text: The doctor searched for the <w>recondite</w> cause of the patient's mysterious illness.
They hiked deep into the forest to find the <w>recondite</w> stream mentioned in the old map.

senses.sense_definition: Avoiding notice; having a tendency to hide or remain shy.

examples.text: The <w>recondite</w> creature is rarely seen by humans because it prefers to stay in the shadows.
Many nocturnal animals have <w>recondite</w> habits that make them difficult to study in the wild.

senses.sense_definition: A scholar or person who has deep mastery over a specialized field.

examples.text: The conference brought together several <w>recondites</w> to discuss the future of theoretical physics.
Only a few <w>recondites</w> truly understood the complexities of the ancient manuscript.

senses.sense_definition: To conceal, cover up, or hide something.

examples.text: The thick fog seemed to <w>recondite</w> the entire valley from our view.
He tried to <w>recondite</w> his true feelings behind a mask of indifference.

traits.comment: This verb usage is largely historical or literary.
